Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 91, Line 8f: "Enter the total of the amounts from Form 8889, lines 16 and 20." Line 20 (Part III, income from failing to remain an eligible individual during a testing period) arises from a qualified HSA funding distribution or from a testing period that began in an earlier year (a last-month-rule testing period that begins in December 2025 cannot be failed in 2025); both are refused by f8889.unsupported ("a qualified HSA funding distribution from an IRA in 2025 ... failing to remain an eligible individual during a testing period that began in an earlier year"), as the line's citation says. Within scope line 20 is zero and person.hsa_taxable is line 16. Same point as the earlier rounds; re-checked on the current scope.yaml, f8889.yaml and s3.yaml this round (the refresh fixes changed only scope.other_income, BUG-0393, and the alimony and educator wording, BUG-0394). Project stands on the English.

Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 93, Line 15: "If you were self-employed and owe self-employment tax, fill in Schedule SE to figure the amount of your deduction." Self-employment income other than Schedule C (farm income on Schedule F, partnership income on a Schedule K-1, church employee income, and since BUG-0233 income as a minister, a member of a religious order who has not taken a vow of poverty, or a Christian Science practitioner) is named in scope.schedule1 ("Any income or adjustment requiring Schedule 1 other than the ones this tool asks about separately ..."), which refuses Form 1040 line 8 and line 10 and every line after them, so within scope only a Schedule C reaches Schedule SE, and person.se_line13 is that deduction. Unchanged by the fix round apart from the clergy wording, which widens the screen. Same point as the earlier rounds; re-checked on the current scope.yaml, f8889.yaml and s3.yaml this round (the refresh fixes changed only scope.other_income, BUG-0393, and the alimony and educator wording, BUG-0394). Project stands on the English.

Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 93, Line 16, "Self-Employed SEP, SIMPLE, and Qualified Plans ... If you were self-employed or a partner, you may be able to take this deduction". Qualified plans other than SEP and SIMPLE are named in scope.schedule1 ("Any income or adjustment requiring Schedule 1 other than the ones this tool asks about separately ..."), which refuses Form 1040 line 8 and line 10 and every line after them ("other qualified retirement plans for the self-employed (such as a solo 401(k) or other Keogh plan)"), and partners are refused there too; within scope person.s16 is the SEP or SIMPLE deduction of a person with a Schedule C, and a filer with a qualified plan answering "none" to person.plan has already answered yes to the screen. Unchanged by fix round 3. Same point as the earlier rounds; re-checked on the current scope.yaml, f8889.yaml and s3.yaml this round (the refresh fixes changed only scope.other_income, BUG-0393, and the alimony and educator wording, BUG-0394). Project stands on the English.

Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 93, Line 17 (self-employed health insurance, Form 7206), which also reaches partners and more-than-2% S corporation shareholders. The screen scope.schedule1 ("Any income or adjustment requiring Schedule 1 other than the ones this tool asks about separately ..."), which refuses Form 1040 line 8 and line 10 and every line after them names "partnerships, S corporations, estates or trusts (Schedule E or a Schedule K-1)", so within scope the deduction arises only from a Schedule C business, which person.sehi computes. Same point as the earlier rounds; re-checked on the current scope.yaml, f8889.yaml and s3.yaml this round (the refresh fixes changed only scope.other_income, BUG-0393, and the alimony and educator wording, BUG-0394). Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 97, IRA Deduction Worksheet line 2: "Single, head of household, or married filing separately and you lived apart from your spouse for all of 2025, enter $89,000 ... Married filing separately and you lived with your spouse at any time in 2025, enter $10,000"; p. 96: "Married persons filing separately. If you weren't covered by a retirement plan but your spouse was, you are considered covered by a plan unless you lived apart from your spouse for all of 2025." The model says the helper uses $10,000 for married filing separately regardless of the line 20 checkbox. Both rules are for married filing separately only, and a married filing separately return is refused at the return level (s3.mfs on scope.ready: "The rules for a married filing separately return ... are outside this tool. Married filing jointly is supported.", i1040gi p. 14). On a joint return the worksheet's own spouse rule ($246,000 for the person not covered) is applied (person.ira_not_covered_joint). Line 20 copies the worksheet total; unchanged by the fix round. Same point as the earlier rounds; re-checked on the current scope.yaml, f8889.yaml and s3.yaml this round (the refresh fixes changed only scope.other_income, BUG-0393, and the alimony and educator wording, BUG-0394). Project stands on the English.
